newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Match says smoke-free tobacco helps result.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Match says smoke-free tobacco helps result.

text.p: Match and cigarette maker Swedish Match on Monday posted a 15 percent fall in profits for the first nine months of 1996, saying sales of smoke-free products were growing in importance for the company.
It said pre-tax profit fell to 1.04 billion crowns ($157.9 million) in the first nine months of the year compared to the same period in 1995. Sales fell to 5.44 billion crowns from 5.54 billion.
But Swedish Match said that its profit before non-recurring items rose 19 percent to 1.22 billion crowns, boosted by sales in Nordic and U.S. markets.

"The improvement in these divisions is in part due to increased sales of smoke-free tobacco products which now account for 27 percent of the company's sales," managing director Goran Linden said in a statement.
The company said it was more cushioned from a fall in cigarette sales than other tobacco companies because of production of moist tobacco products such as chewing tobacco.
"In the United States where legal actions against cigarette companies are common and often affect the view of the tobacco industry, we sell almost no cigarettes," Linden said.
Its lighter and match unit was hurt by lower margins due to competitive prices on certain markets.
Next year's result will reflect lower costs following the closing of tobacco plants in Sweden and Estonia and a matchstick plant in Hungary.
A stronger currency hurt the firm's result.
"The stronger crown has negatively affected sales by 350 million crowns," the company said.

Swedish Match made its debut on the Stockholm bourse and Nasdaq in New York in May this year after its former owner, Swedish vehicle group Volvo AB, decided to hand out Swedish Match shares to shareholders in the form of a dividend.
Swedish Match shares were unchanged at 1300 GMT at 19.50 crowns.
-- Abigail Schmelz, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1003 ($ = 6.587 Swedish Crowns)
